body:
## Basis

The repo has no commit containing this implementation (`git log` = `init` / `Initial commit`; every source file is untracked), so the working tree is the review target. I read `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `DIVERGENCES.md`, `plan/03`, `plan/04`, `plan/07`, `plan/10` and all of `crates/rich-editor-auy/src/{model,schema,pos,step,state,wire,a11y,error,motion,math,command}`. I ran `cargo test -p rich-editor-auy` (green) plus a throwaway crate in `/tmp` that drives the public API; no repo file was modified. Every finding below was reproduced at runtime unless marked `[static]`.

**Verdict: `incorrect`.** The algebra is not sound: multi-step undo corrupts text, four of six step variants fail `apply(invert(step))` in reachable cases, selection mapping can leave the document, `Doc::validate` accepts documents that cannot be serialized, the wire parser can abort the process, and a fresh `EditorState` cannot be edited at all. None of this is listed in `DIVERGENCES.md`.

---

## Direct answers

**(1) Does `apply(invert(step))` hold for every implemented variant? — No.**

| Variant | Result |
|---|---|
| `Replace` (structural fragment) | Holds for block-aligned ranges (join/split undo verified). |
| `Replace` (plain text) | Holds for same-block, atom-free ranges. **Fails silently for ranges containing an inline atom** (forward keeps the atom, inverse drops it). |
| `ReplaceAround` | Inverse holds (verified by `editing.rs`), but `step_map()` is wrong, so state-level selection after split is wrong. |
| `AddMark` | **Fails when the mark is already present**: inverse is an unconditional `RemoveMark`, so the “inverse” removes a mark the original had. |
| `RemoveMark` | **Fails when the mark is absent**: inverse is an unconditional `AddMark`; state undo actually *adds* the mark (reproduced). |
| `SetNodeAttr` | **Fails when the previous value was absent** (default omitted): inverse is `Null`, which `validate_attrs` rejects, so undo errors; `set_node_id(at, None)` always errors. |
| `SetDocAttr` | **Fails when the previous value was absent**: undo writes `"lang":null`, producing a document `from_json` can no longer decode. |

**(2) Are structural `Replace`/join/split ranges and inverses correct?** Mostly for the block-aligned cases: `replace_blocks` requires `from` at a block start and `to` at a block end, and `blocks_between`/`invert_step` reconstruct the removed blocks; join and split undo work. But: block **deletion** is inexpressible (`replace()` routes an empty fragment to the text path and errors), `join_backward` sets the caret one position past the join and merges blocks of different kinds without normalizing runs or reporting the discarded ID (plan I17), and `ReplaceAround::step_map` is wrong.

**(3) Does selection mapping stay in range? — No.** Splitting `"abcde"` (size 7) at `Pos(6)` yields a caret at `Pos(14)` on a document of size 9 (I15 violated). Cause: `step_map()` for `ReplaceAround`. `Selection::map` also falls back to the *old* position on mapping failure and nothing clamps the explicit selection.

**(4) Is `Doc::validate` sound? — No.** It passes a `Text` payload on a block-only kind, passes inline atoms with undeclared kinds/attrs, passes mark attrs with undeclared ids, passes undeclared root attrs — all of which make the canonical writer fail. It correctly catches I1/I2 (Blocks payloads), I3/I4, I6 (allowed/excludes), I7 (block attrs), I8, I10 and I16.

**(5) Does the wire parser preserve offsets/paths? — No.** The JSON tokenizer localizes syntax errors, but every semantic error hard-codes `offset: 0`; nested paths use `"0.1"` while `DocPath` uses `"0/1"`; the limit error derives its offset from the error message length; valid `\uD83D\uDE00` surrogate pairs are rejected; and object/array nesting has no depth limit — 20 000 nested arrays abort the process with stack overflow.

**(6) Are a11y ranges/order/names consistent?** Ranges and order are consistent (block range includes the node’s tokens, text ranges are the byte ranges, atoms are 1). Names/roles are not: `MarkSpec.a11y` is never consumed and `href` is read from a mark literally named `"link"`, so link nodes never get `A11yRole::Link` and `A002` is unreachable; issue paths are tree indices that drift from document paths (`A001` reported at path `"2"` for document block index 1).

---

## Findings (prioritized)

### P0

**1. Multi-step undo applies inverses in forward order — `[bug]`**
`src/state/mod.rs:142` reverses the inverse vector (`inverse.reverse()`), and `src/state/history.rs:122` then iterates `group.inverse.iter().rev()`. The two reversals cancel, so inverses are applied in step order. Reproduced: replace `"bc"` with `"XY"` in `"abcd"` (delete + insert), undo returns `"aXYd"`; two inserts `"A"` then `"B"` undo to `"Bbcd"` instead of `"abcd"`. Plan §9 says inverses are applied in reverse order; I14 fails. Minimal fix:
```rust
for step in &group.inverse {
    current = apply_step(&current, schema, step).map_err(EditError::Step)?;
}
```

### P1

**2. `ReplaceAround::step_map` computes `new_len = from + insert` — `[bug]`**
`src/step/mod.rs:156-162`. For a split at `Pos(6)` with `insert = 2`, `StepMap::replacement(6, 0, 8)` shifts every later position by 8 instead of 2: caret `6` maps to `14` in a document of size 9. Plan I15 (“`map` never points past the result document”) fails; `ChangeSet` (`state/change.rs:79`) uses the correct value, so the two disagree. Minimal fix: pass `*insert` as `new_len`.

**3. `AddMark`/`RemoveMark` inverses are unconditional — `[bug]`**
`src/step/invert.rs:60-68` returns the opposite step unconditionally, and `Step::is_noop` (`src/step/mod.rs:172-179`) only tests `from == to`, so a mark step that changes nothing is still recorded with an inverse that does. Reproduced at state level: removing an absent `strong` from `"abcd"` succeeds unchanged, then undo produces `{"text":"ab","marks":[{"type":"strong"}]}`; adding an already-present mark and inverting removes it. Minimal fix: only record an inverse when the applied step changed the document (compare `doc` before/after) or make `invert` return a no-op when the range does not carry/need the mark.

**4. `SetNodeAttr` inverse uses `Null` for absent attributes — `[bug]`**
`src/step/invert.rs:70-77` uses `unwrap_or(AttrValue::Null)`; `set_node_attr` (`src/step/apply.rs:177-205`) then validates the value against `AttrType` (`src/schema/mod.rs:198-215`), which rejects `Null` for `Str`/`Int`/`Bool`. Reproduced: set `heading.level = 3` (previous value omitted, schema default 1), undo returns `Err("... attr_type")`. `set_node_id(Pos(1), None)` has the same defect and always errors, so IDs cannot be cleared. Minimal fix: treat `AttrValue::Null` as attribute removal in `set_node_attr` (`block.attrs().without(attr)` when the value is `Null`) and in the inverse path, so undo restores the absent/default state.

**5. `SetDocAttr` ignores the schema and inverts to `Null` — `[bug]` + `[plan violation]`**
`src/step/apply.rs:213-231` takes `_schema` and never validates the attr against `DocSpec::attrs`; `src/step/invert.rs:78-81` inverts to `Null`. Reproduced: `set_doc_attr(lang, "pt-BR")`, undo → `{"type":"doc","attrs":{"lang":null},...}`, and `from_json` fails with `expected_string`. Plan §3.4 requires root attrs to be declared/validated; `Schema::validate_attrs` has no doc-level equivalent. Minimal fix: validate the attr id/type against `schema.doc().attrs` (reject undeclared ids) and use the same Null-means-remove rule as finding 4.

**6. `EditorState::new` produces an invalid document that cannot accept edits — `[bug]` + `[plan violation]`**
`src/state/mod.rs:61-74` builds `Doc::from_blocks(Attrs::empty(), Vec::new())`. With the preset `doc { content: "block+" }`, that doc already fails `Doc::validate` (I1), and both `insert_text(Pos(1), …)` and `insert_text(Pos(0), …)` fail with `OutOfBounds { position: 1, size: 0 }`. This is exactly the documented usage in plan §13 (`EditorState::new(schema)` then `tx.insert_text(Pos(1), "Olá, mundo")`). Minimal fix: construct the initial document through the schema (insert the first accepted block, e.g. the `filler` kind as an empty text block) or require the caller to pass an initial `Doc`.

**7. Block-boundary and end-of-document ranges are rejected by the text path — `[bug]`**
`src/step/apply.rs:68-100` rejects `from`/`to` on a block’s open token (`local_start == 0`, line 84) and any `to` past the block’s content (`text_range`). Reproduced: `delete(0..doc.size())` → `Err("replace_structural_token")`; `insert_text(Pos(doc.size()), "x")` → `Err("text_range")`. Consequently `select_all` (`src/command/mod.rs:89-93`) followed by `delete_selection`/`insert_text` can never apply, and typing at the canonical end-of-document position (`plan/04` §3.3 marks it as a valid caret) is impossible. Minimal fix: normalize boundary positions into the adjacent block (treat `from == block_start` as content offset 0 of that block; treat `to == doc.size()` as the last block’s content end) and route whole-document/block-aligned deletes through `replace_blocks`.

**8. Unbounded recursion in the JSON parser and decoder — `[bug]`**
`src/wire/json_parser.rs:44-54` (`value()` recurses for every array/object) and `src/wire/parser.rs:67-146` (`decode_block` recurses with nesting) have no depth guard; `Limits::max_depth` (`src/lib.rs:50`) is never read. Reproduced: 20 000 nested `[` abort with stack overflow (`exit=134`); a deeply nested (valid) `bullet_list`/`list_item` document does the same. Plan §10 “no panic on untrusted input” and `AGENTS.md` rule 2 are violated (an abort is worse than a panic; fuzz was never run — `DIVERGENCES` H). Minimal fix: thread a `depth` parameter through `Parser::value`/`decode_block`, bounded by a constant or `options.limits.max_depth`, returning `ParseError`.

**9. `Doc::validate` misses payload, atom, mark-attr and root-attr invariants — `[bug]`**
`src/model/validate.rs:96-124` only checks run emptiness/ceiling/adjacency and mark permissions for `BlockContent::Text`; `InlineItem::Atom` is reduced to `previous = None`, so the atom’s `kind`, `atom`/`inline` flags and attrs are never validated. `validate_marks` (`:158-179`) never validates mark attributes with `Schema::validate_attrs`, and `Doc::validate` never validates `self.attrs()` against `DocSpec::attrs`. Reproduced (each returns `issues == []` while `to_json_string`/`write_doc_into` fails with `fmt::Error`): a `paragraph` containing `InlineAtom { kind: NodeKind(999) }`; a run whose `strong` carries attr id 9; a doc with root attr id 7; a `bullet_list` built with a `TextBlock` payload. Minimal fix: dispatch on the payload type against the node spec (text block ⇔ content expression admits inline kinds; container ⇔ block kinds), validate each inline atom kind/attrs, validate each mark set with `schema.validate_attrs`, and validate root attrs.

**10. The decoder infers the block payload from the children instead of the schema — `[bug]`**
`src/wire/parser.rs:104-116`: `children.iter().all(...spec.inline)` is vacuously true for an empty `content: []`, so an empty container such as `{"type":"bullet_list","content":[]}` is decoded as a `TextBlock`; `Doc::validate` then accepts it (finding 9) and the writer re-emits it. A missing `content` key (`:92`) likewise yields a text block for any non-atom kind, and `spec.atom` (`:89`) silently discards provided children. Minimal fix: derive the shape from `NodeSpec` (atom / text / container) rather than from the parsed children, and reject (or filler-fill) empty containers per plan §6.

**11. `Doc::to_json_string` silently returns an empty string on failure — `[bug]`**
`src/wire/mod.rs:34-45`: `write_doc_into` returns `fmt::Error` for unknown node kinds/attr ids (findings 9’s inputs), and `to_json_string` converts that into `String::new()`. A consumer persisting that value writes an empty document with no error. The doc comment (“the writer for a `String` is infallible”) is false. Minimal fix: return `Result<String, fmt::Error>` (or a `WireError`) and propagate; do not fall back to `""`.

### P2

**12. The decoder normalizes runs with the block byte limit, not `MAX_RUN_BYTES` — `[bug]`**
`src/wire/parser.rs:118` calls `text.normalize(options.limits.max_block_text_bytes)` (default 1 MiB), while `MAX_RUN_BYTES` is 4096 and plan §3.1/§6/I4 require runs ≤ 4 KiB. Reproduced: a 5000-byte `text` node parses into one 5000-byte run and `Doc::validate` reports I4, so `from_json` returns a document that its own validator rejects. Minimal fix: normalize with `u32::try_from(MAX_RUN_BYTES)`, and apply `max_block_text_bytes` as a block-level check.

**13. Schema fingerprint omits semantic declarations — `[bug]`**
`src/schema/builder.rs:227-278` hashes doc content, doc attrs (id/name/kind/required), node name/kind/content/groups/marks/inline and node attrs (id/name/kind/required), mark name/id/`inclusive` and mark attrs. It omits `NodeSpec.atom`, `defining`, `isolating`, mark `excludes`, every `A11ySpec` (role/name/alt/level) and every `AttrSpec.default`. Reproduced: schemas differing only in `MarkSpec::excludes("strong")`, or only in a mark’s `A11ySpec`, produce the identical fingerprint `2cfb199…`. `Envelope::from_json` (`src/wire/envelope.rs:84-90`) therefore accepts documents written under a schema with different mark-conflict or a11y semantics — the `SchemaMismatch` guard the plan (§8.2, F24) assigns to the fingerprint does not work. Minimal fix: include every semantic field, canonically formatted (avoid `{:?}` for the long-term wire-stable hash).

**14. An `Int` attribute accepts an empty array — `[bug]`**
`src/schema/mod.rs:205`: `(AttrType::Int { .. }, AttrValue::Array(values)) => values.is_empty()`. Reproduced via the public API: `set_node_attr(heading, level, Array([]))` applies, `Doc::validate` passes, the writer emits `"level":[]`, and `from_json` then fails with `expected_int`. Minimal fix: delete that arm.

**15. `MarkSpec.a11y` is declared, validated, and never used — `[bug]` + `[plan violation]`**
`src/a11y/build.rs:130-145` always emits `A11yRole::Text` for runs and reads `href` via `mark_attr(schema, &run.marks, "link", "href")` (`:141`), a hard-coded schema name; `schema/index`-level mark a11y is only touched in `schema/builder.rs` validation. Reproduced with a mark named `link2` carrying `A11ySpec::new(A11yRole::Link)`: the tree shows `Text`, `href: None`, and `validate_a11y` reports no `A002` — so link semantics and A4 are unreachable. Plan/10 §3 and “o schema é a fonte dos roles” are violated. Minimal fix: in `child_nodes`, look up `schema.mark(id).a11y` and build the node role/name/href from it (no literal `"link"`).

**16. a11y issue paths are tree indices, not document paths — `[bug]`**
`src/a11y/validate.rs:29-45` numbers `tree.root.children`; `src/a11y/build.rs:28-38` receives the document `DocPath` but never stores it, and promotes the children of a block whose `A11ySpec` is `None`. Reproduced: with a paragraph without `A11ySpec` (two runs) followed by an image (doc block index 1), `A001` reports path `"2"`. `Doc::validate` and `ParseError` use document paths, so the same `DocPath` type means different things. Plan I19/D62 require `path`. Minimal fix: store the document `DocPath` on `A11yNode` (or a parallel path vector) and report it.

**17. IME composition updates accumulate text — `[bug]`**
`src/state/transaction_meta.rs:24-38`: `CompositionEvent::Update` always replaces `composition_range` (the range supplied at `Start`) and never advances it. Reproduced: `Start{3..3}`, `Update "k"`, `Update "ka"` yields `"abkak"` instead of `"abka"`. Minimal fix after pushing the step: `self.composition_range = Some(Range::new(range.start, range.start.checked_add(u32::try_from(text.len())...)))`.

**18. `toggle_mark` decides from `stored_marks`, so it cannot remove a range mark — `[bug]`**
`src/command/mod.rs:54-75` sets `active = state.stored_marks().contains(mark.id)` and never inspects the selected text. Reproduced with the preset: three consecutive `toggle_mark(same strong)` calls on `1..3` leave `strong` applied every time. Minimal fix: for a non-empty range, query whether the range already carries the mark (a `Doc` scan of runs in the range) and choose add/remove from that.

**19. `replace_text` keeps an inline atom when the range ends on the atom — `[bug]`**
`src/step/text_edit.rs:78-92`: after `cursor = run_end`, the branch `else if cursor >= end` is taken for an atom exactly covering `[p, p+1)`, so the atom is preserved and the inserted text is placed *before* it. Reproduced on `a[image]b`: `Replace{2..3, "X"}` → `"aX", image, "b"` (atom not deleted); `Replace{1..3, "X"}` → `"X"` + image + `"b"`. Minimal fix: capture the atom start before advancing (`let atom_start = cursor;`) and branch on `atom_start >= end` for “after range”, `run_end <= start` for “before”, else drop the atom.

**20. `SetNodeAttr` targets the top-level ancestor, and out-of-range positions are accepted — `[bug]`**
`src/step/apply.rs:177-199` uses `locate`, which only resolves top-level blocks (`src/model/doc.rs:158-167`); nested blocks are never targeted. Reproduced: `set_node_id(Pos(3), "inner")` in `bullet_list(list_item(paragraph("hi")))` sets the id on the `bullet_list`. `Doc::block_at` also returns the last block for any `pos >= last.start`, so `set_node_attr(Pos(999), …)` on a 3-byte doc succeeds instead of returning `OutOfBounds`. Minimal fix: have `locate` return the innermost block plus its path/offset (and reject positions `> doc.size()`), and rebuild the ancestor chain on replacement.

**21. `ChangeSet` reports an empty new range for structural `Replace` — `[bug]`**
`src/state/change.rs:64-70` uses `slice.text.len()` for the new length; structural slices carry their blocks in `slice.content` and have empty `text`. Reproduced: joining `"a"` + `"b"` yields `RangeChange { old: 0..6, new: 0..0 }` although the merged block occupies `0..4`. Plan/10 A10 and §4 rule 6 need the announcement range; use `replace_len(slice)` (`step::apply`’s helper already handles both paths).

**22. `Limits` fields are unenforced and autofill/productivity are absent — `[plan violation]`**
`max_depth`, `max_runs_per_block`, `max_attrs_per_node`, `max_attr_string_bytes`, `max_mark_attrs` are declared in `src/lib.rs:44-74` and never read (only `max_doc_bytes`/`max_nodes` in `Doc::new`, and `max_block_text_bytes` is misused as the run ceiling). `SchemaError::NonProductive` and `LimitError::Depth/BlockTextBytes/AttrStringBytes` are never constructed; `Schema::filler` (`src/schema/mod.rs:128-133`) has no caller, so plan §6 normalization/autofill (filler for required-empty containers, attribute defaults/omission, productivity check in §3.4 step 4) is not implemented and not registered in `DIVERGENCES.md`. Minimal fix: enforce each limit in `Doc::new`/`from_json`, implement the filler in step application, and add the mandatory-cycle check to `SchemaBuilder::build`.

**23. Mark `excludes` is not applied when adding a mark — `[bug]`**
`src/step/apply.rs:104-152` (`mark_range`) and `src/step/text_edit.rs:210-262` only add/remove the requested mark; the exclusion closure is checked only later by `Doc::validate`. Reproduced with `em.excludes("strong")`: `AddMark(strong)` then `AddMark(em)` on `1..3` succeeds and produces `marks:[{strong},{em}]`, flagged I6 only by a separate validation call. Plan I6 assigns this to `add_mark`/normalize. Minimal fix: after adding a mark, remove every excluded mark from the same range.

**24. `join_backward` sets the caret one position past the join and merges unlike kinds — `[bug]` + `[plan violation]`**
`src/state/transaction_join.rs:46` sets `Selection::caret(at)` where `at` is the *pre-join* block boundary; after the join the equivalent position is `at - 1` (reproduced: joining `"a"`+`"b"` yields caret `3`, the merged block’s close-token position; typing there appends after `"b"` instead of between `"a"` and `"b"`). `:83-89` merges with `TextBlock::push` and no `norma…
